xBRIEFInfo.description: Plan for PAN-5649: Opening an idle-stopped workspace app starts its stack again: Traefik fallback wake page and a dashboard start-app action

plan.title: Opening an idle-stopped workspace app starts its stack again: Traefik fallback wake page and a dashboard start-app action
plan.author: agent:claude-opus-5-5

narratives.Problem: After PAN-5250 idle-stops a workspace's frontend, its app URL returns Traefik's 404 and the Command Deck app chip links to that 404. Only pan workspace up, a spawn or a verification brings it back, so the operator's bookmark and a work agent's own Playwright or curl check fail.
narratives.Proposal: A lowest-priority Traefik router (separate dynamic file workspace-wake.yml, written by generateOverdeckTraefikConfig and by the dashboard at startup) sends feature-<issue>.<domain> hosts to the dashboard when no frontend router matches. The wake router's middleware adds an X-Overdeck-Wake-Router marker; the dashboard consumes only marked feature-host requests in a raw host-dispatched handler (knowledge-viewer pattern, wired before the terminal upgrade handler), accepts only trusted local callers, wakes only on navigations or header-less clients through a per-issue coordinator around wakeWorkspaceStack (trigger browser), redirects to the container's label host when it differs, and answers 503 + Retry-After with a self-contained page that reloads once the status path stops being answered by the dashboard. A new POST /api/workspaces/:issueId/wake (no route-scope row, so admin) backs a start app button in the Command Deck row. Docs and changelog replace the PAN-5250 gap notes.
narratives.NonGoals:
- Projects whose workspace hosts are served by a Traefik other than the managed overdeck-traefik container
- Waking from api-feature-<issue> hosts or any host not starting with feature-
- Changing the operator's projects.yaml (pan.localhost for overdeck) or workspace-data.ts frontendUrl derivation
- Waiting server-side for the app to be ready
- Waking from subresource, fetch or WebSocket requests
- Any credential or token for the wake host
- Changing the old reaper, the idle-stop rules or the restore door's container selection
- Changing overdeck.yml.template
- Touching src/dashboard/server/main.ts
- A route-scopes.ts row and telemetry client-route entry for the wake route
- Dispatching on Host shape without the Traefik marker header

autoDecisions.summary: Auth: trusted local caller only (isTrustedLocalCaller via a raw-Node adapter), no token
autoDecisions.rationale: Agent curl/Playwright checks and bookmarks carry no token; the same rule already mints a full session, and the wake grants strictly less. Funnel and LAN get 404.

autoDecisions.summary: Only navigations and header-less clients wake; subresources, fetch and WebSocket never do
autoDecisions.rationale: Blocks cross-site wakes and stale-tab HMR pings while keeping curl, Playwright and page loads working.

autoDecisions.summary: Wake router in a separate dynamic file written by both generateOverdeckTraefikConfig and the dashboard at startup
autoDecisions.rationale: pan reload never re-renders Traefik config; the dashboard-side write makes the deploy path carry the router with no mode-dependent content.

autoDecisions.summary: Domain-agnostic HostRegexp ^feature-… with a dashboard-side wake-domain check
autoDecisions.rationale: One router covers every project domain on the shared Traefik without re-rendering; anchoring on feature- cannot shadow knowledge-, artifacts. or api-feature- hosts.

autoDecisions.summary: Redirect to the frontend container's label host when it differs from the request host
autoDecisions.rationale: The overdeck project's dns.domain (pan.localhost) disagrees with the compose template (overdeck.localhost); without the redirect the page would reload forever on an unrouted host.

autoDecisions.summary: Answer 503 + Retry-After immediately instead of holding the request
autoDecisions.rationale: curl -f fails until ready, curl --retry retries, Playwright goto does not throw, and no request is held for container start time.

autoDecisions.summary: New journal-aware POST /api/workspaces/:issueId/wake instead of reusing stack/start
autoDecisions.rationale: stack/start runs docker compose start with no lock and no stack.restored entry, leaving the open reclaim open.

autoDecisions.summary: Start app button opens the tab synchronously, then POSTs
autoDecisions.rationale: window.open after an await is popup-blocked; the opened tab lands on the wake page, which waits and reloads.

autoDecisions.summary: Start app also shows for a fully stopped stack; unhealthy keeps no chip
autoDecisions.rationale: The wake starts old-reaper stops too; a crashed stack should not be papered over.

autoDecisions.summary: Browser wakes restore gate-starvation reclaims too (same as pan workspace up)
autoDecisions.rationale: The app needs its api; stale tabs cannot trigger a wake, so only explicit intent restores.

autoDecisions.summary: Dispatch only requests carrying the Traefik-set X-Overdeck-Wake-Router marker
autoDecisions.rationale: Overdeck workspace stacks run this dashboard server behind a Vite /ws proxy without changeOrigin, so their WebSocket upgrades arrive with feature-… Hosts; Host-only dispatch would break them.

autoDecisions.summary: No route-scopes.ts row for the wake route (unlisted = admin)
autoDecisions.rationale: Any row also requires TELEMETRY_CLIENT_ROUTES and docs/TELEMETRY.md changes (route-scopes.test.ts:82); only the desktop Command Deck calls the route, and every browser session is admin. The issue named route-scopes.ts; this records the deviation.

autoDecisions.summary: Vite ping requests on wake hosts fail (WebSocket 503, text/x-vite-ping socket destroyed)
autoDecisions.rationale: A stale tab must never turn its reconnect ping into a reload-navigation that wakes the stack or undoes a memory reclaim.

metadata.acJustification: Security boundary with six independently observable behaviors (trust, validation, waking rules, redirect/status, dedupe, dispatch scope).
metadata.parallelSafeReason: It owns its own new files plus two single-line edits (dashboard-auth.ts, server.ts) no other wave-1 item touches; its only file overlap is with wi4b, which a blocks edge serializes after it.

narrative.Action: Implement PRD WI-4 steps 1, 2 (everything except the REST route), the setupWorkspaceWakeHost line of step 3, and the step-6 tests except REST-route ones: isTrustedLocalNodeRequest in dashboard-auth.ts; in new routes/workspace-wake.ts the coordinator (requestWorkspaceWake with in-flight join and 15 s TTL, never rejects; getWorkspaceWakeStatus; resolveAppHost with 60 s cache), handleWakeHostRequest in the PRD's (a)-(f) order, setupWorkspaceWakeHost mirroring setupKnowledgeViewerProxy but dispatching only isWakeRouterRequest requests/upgrades (marker header + feature host; unmarked requests pass through untouched), destroying Vite-ping sockets, ensureWorkspaceWakeRouterFile (fs/promises, skip when the dynamic dir is missing, write only on change), wakePollDecision and renderWakePage (escaped, CSP header). Call setupWorkspaceWakeHost(nodeServer) right after holdRequestsUntilServed(nodeServer) and before setupTerminalWebSocket(nodeServer) in server.ts. Never touch main.ts.

items.title: Given a marked request with Host 'feature-pan-1.overdeck.localhost' from an untrusted peer, the handler returns 404 'Not found'; a trusted marked request for domain 'evil.test' or an unregistered project returns 404; neither wake nor readLabelHost is called in these cases

Given a trusted marked request with no sec-fetch-mode, the handler returns 503 with 'Retry-After: 5' and 'x-overdeck-wake: 1' and calls wake once with trigger 'browser'; a 'no-cors' request returns 503 without calling wake, and an Accept 'text/x-vite-ping' request gets its socket destroyed with no status line

Given label host 'feature-pan-1.overdeck.localhost' and request host 'feature-pan-1.pan.localhost', the handler returns 307 to 'https://feature-pan-1.overdeck.localhost/x?y=1' without calling wake; GET /__overdeck_wake/status returns 200 JSON with 'state' and 'x-overdeck-wake' and never calls wake
When two requestWorkspaceWake calls run concurrently, wake runs once; a call 10 s after completion returns the cached result and a call 16 s after completion starts a new wake (fake timers)

When a request or /ws/rpc upgrade has Host 'feature-pan-1.overdeck.localhost' but no x-overdeck-wake-router marker, it routes to the original listeners unchanged; a marked upgrade receives a 503 status line and an upgrade listener registered after setupWorkspaceWakeHost never sees it
ensureWorkspaceWakeRouterFile returns 'skipped' for a missing dynamic dir, 'written' on first call in a temp dir and 'unchanged' on the second

metadata.sizeJustification: 22 files, within the 25-file limit. The subsystem count (9) comes from path-shaped docs (docs/, guides/, cli/, two changelog.d files each count separately) and two test roots; production code lives only in src/lib and src/dashboard. The issue is already the browser half split out of PAN-5250; the wake page, its REST route and the chip that opens it share one coordinator and one contract, so splitting further would ship a chip whose opened tab still 404s or a route nothing calls.
